Series::index_put_¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signatures¶

Series::index_put_(pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<Series> indices, const Series& values, bool accumulate) const -> Series&
Series::index_put_(std::initializer_list<Series> indices, const Series& values, bool accumulate) const -> Series&
Series::index_put_(std::int64_t index, const Series& values, bool accumulate = false) const -> Series&
Series::index_put_(std::initializer_list<ExtractSpec> specs, const Series& values, bool accumulate = false) const -> Series&

What It Does¶

Mutates the series through explicit index-based writes and returns *this.

This method family is intentionally broader than one signature suggests:

  • the Series index-list overloads are the general advanced-index write path

  • the scalar std::int64_t overload is an explicit 1D convenience

  • the ExtractSpec initializer-list overload is a narrow convenience layer for common 1D and 2D write forms

The accumulate toggle belongs to the general advanced-index form. When it is false, matching positions are replaced. When it is true, matching positions are incremented instead.

One API quirk is worth saying explicitly: the method is declared const on the handle, but it still mutates the underlying storage. On this surface, handle constness does not imply value immutability.

Parameters¶

indices (pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<Series> or std::initializer_list<Series>)

The explicit advanced index tensors for the general overloads.

Use these when you already have integer index series and want the most direct advanced-index write path. This is the only overload family here that supports accumulate=true.

index (std::int64_t)

The scalar convenience form. This overload is intentionally 1D-only and requires a scalar values.

specs (std::initializer_list<ExtractSpec>)

The constrained slice-spec convenience layer.

This overload supports exactly two handwritten convenience shapes:

  • x.index_put_({i}, scalar_value) on 1D input

  • x.index_put_({SliceAll(), j}, column_values) on 2D input

For anything richer, use extract_put_() or the general Series index-list overloads.

values (const Series&)

The write source.

Accepted cardinality depends on the overload family:

  • scalar convenience requires a scalar source

  • 2D ExtractSpec column convenience requires a 1D source of length size(0)

  • general Series index-list writes follow the backend advanced-index write rules; common usage is one value per indexed position, or scalar broadcast where supported

accumulate (bool)

  • false: replace written positions

  • true: add into written positions

This toggle is unsupported on the ExtractSpec convenience overload.

Returns¶

Series& The same mutated series handle.

Examples¶

Example 1. The initializer-list Series overload is the shortest way to do a basic advanced-index write.

auto vec = pluss::make_series(std::vector<double>{0, 1, 2, 3, 4}, {5});
auto idx = pluss::make_series(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 3}, {2});
auto picked = pluss::make_series(std::vector<double>{90, 70}, {2});

vec.index_put_({idx}, picked, false);

std::cout << vec;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 90, 2, 70, 4]

Example 2. The RangeView overload is the same engine, but useful when the index list already lives in a container. Here accumulate=true adds into the existing positions instead of replacing them.

auto dup_idx = pluss::make_series(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 1, 3}, {3});
auto dup_values = pluss::make_series(std::vector<double>{10, 20, 30}, {3});
std::vector<pluss::Series> indices{dup_idx};

vec.index_put_(
    pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<pluss::Series>(indices),
    dup_values,
    true);

std::cout << vec;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 120, 2, 100, 4]

Because index 1 appears twice, both 10 and 20 are accumulated into the existing 90.

Example 3. The scalar convenience overload is intentionally 1D-only and expects a scalar source.

vec.index_put_(0, pluss::codem::value(-5.0));
std::cout << vec;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[-5, 120, 2, 100, 4]

Example 4. The 1D ExtractSpec convenience form accepts a single scalar index specifier.

vec.index_put_({std::int64_t{2}}, pluss::codem::value(555.0));
std::cout << vec;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[-5, 120, 555, 100, 4]

Example 5. The 2D ExtractSpec convenience form is for whole-column replacement: {SliceAll(), j} plus a length-size(0) source vector.

auto mat = pluss::make_series(
    std::vector<double>{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9},
    {3, 3});
auto col_values = pluss::make_series(std::vector<double>{30, 60, 90}, {3});

mat.index_put_({pluss::Slicing::SliceAll(), std::int64_t{2}}, col_values);

std::cout << mat;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=9, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 2, 30],
  [4, 5, 60],
  [7, 8, 90]]

Example 6. accumulate=true is rejected on the slice-spec convenience overload, because that overload is intentionally narrow.

try {
  mat.index_put_({pluss::Slicing::SliceAll(), std::int64_t{1}}, col_values, true);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string msg = e.what();
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n'));
}

Output¶

Series::index_put_(specs, value, accumulate): accumulate=true is unsupported for slice-spec indexing; use Series index list overload instead

Notes¶

  • Reach for the Series index-list overloads when you want the real advanced indexing surface, especially if accumulate matters.

  • Reach for the ExtractSpec convenience overload only for the narrow 1D/2D shorthand it was designed for.

  • For richer selector-based writes, extract_put_() is usually easier to read than constructing index tensors by hand.
